subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should Telegram/ACP source turns enforce action-verification or fail-closed behavior when visible final text claims side effects without matching tool evidence?
rationale: Current main has narrow message-tool-only diagnostics, but choosing whether and how to verify arbitrary claimed side effects affects channel UX, privacy, fallback behavior, and existing direct-message semantics.

options.title: Define verification policy
options.body: Require a tool-result-backed ledger or explicit diagnostics before delivering visible success claims on Telegram/ACP turns.

options.title: Keep scope to delivery-tool gaps
options.body: Treat #85714-style missing message-tool delivery as the only platform-owned fix and leave broader claim verification to agent prompts/hooks.

options.title: Document current boundary
options.body: Document that OpenClaw transports final text but does not verify arbitrary side effects unless a future plugin or hook supplies that policy.

recommendation.title: Define verification policy
recommendation.body: Require a tool-result-backed ledger or explicit diagnostics before delivering visible success claims on Telegram/ACP turns.

likelyOwner.reason: The nearest merged source-reply policy PR was maintainer-rewritten and merged by steipete, making them the strongest available owner signal for the product boundary choice.
